nodes.title: SG-3.3 · Switch BootScene and components to the input layer
nodes.body:
Context: game/frontend/src/phaser/input.ts already exports createInputLayer (focus, moveFocus, keydown, hover, click, destroy), but BootScene.ts still registers its own onKeyDown, onInteract and onHoverChange handlers, binds the character pointerdown itself, and ObjectOverlay.tsx emits menuClose from its own onKeyDown. Desired behavior: every key and pointer action for object focus, interaction and menuClose goes through the input layer, which emits through the typed bridge. Expected result: no ad hoc handlers remain, gameplay is unchanged, and cleanup runs on scene shutdown. Why: SG-3 asks for a single input layer.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given BootScene.create has run, When a key is pressed, Then only the input layer's keydown handler is registered with the keyboard plugin and it is removed when the scene shuts down
- Given the scene has shut down, When a key, hover or click happens, Then no bridge event is emitted
- Given the bootSceneKeyboard, bootSceneHover and bootSceneFocus tests, When they run, Then they assert behaviour (events emitted, focus state, teardown) and pass without deletion or skipping
- Given npm test and npm run typecheck, When run in game/ and game/frontend/, Then both pass


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene.ts key, hover, click and character pointer wiring
- In scope: ObjectOverlay Escape handling
- In scope: Rewriting the three BootScene input test groups
- Out of scope: New features, content or juice
- Out of scope: backend/ and frontend/src/api/client.ts
- Out of scope: SG-3.1 and SG-3.2 work
- Preserve: Player-visible behaviour
- Preserve: Store-driven focus sync in BootScene.applyFocusedObject
- Preserve: Phaser ~3.90.0 pin


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays pinned at ~3.90.0 and the phaser-pin guard test keeps passing
- No source file in game/src or game/frontend/src is over 200 lines
- game/src never imports from game/frontend
- The Zustand store is the only owner of GameState
- No test is deleted or skipped; tests mock only what is external
- npm test and npm run typecheck pass in game/ and game/frontend/


## Definition of done
- All requirements delivered and verified
- Both test suites and typechecks pass


## Non-functional requirements
- Listeners released on scene shutdown and component unmount


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · BootScene routes keyboard, hover, click and focus through the input layer and destroys it on shutdown
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene.create registers onInteract/onHoverChange per object and this.input.keyboard.on('keydown', this.onKeyDown) duplicating input.ts. Desired: create() calls createInputLayer(this.input, this.sceneObjects); SHUTDOWN calls its destroy(). Result: one handler path, identical behaviour. Why: single input layer.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given create() ran, When Tab, arrows, Enter, Space or Escape is pressed, Then focusChange, interaction or menuClose is emitted exactly once as before
- Given an object is hovered or clicked, When the pointer fires, Then objectHover or objectClick is emitted once
- Given SHUTDOWN ran, When the same events fire, Then nothing is emitted and keyboard.off was called with the registered handler


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene.ts
- Out of scope: Character pointer handling
- Out of scope: ObjectOverlay
- Preserve: applyFocusedObject store-to-scene sync
- Preserve: Transition and animation subscriptions


## Technical constraints
- Phaser ~3.90.0 pin
- BootScene.ts stays under 200 lines
- Zustand store owns GameState


## Dependencies
- game/frontend/src/phaser/input.ts createInputLayer


## Definition of done
- BootScene has no onKeyDown, focusedObjectIdFromScene or direct keyboard.on/off
- Layer destroyed in SHUTDOWN


## Non-functional requirements
- No per-frame allocations added


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: Add `export interface PointerTarget { on(e: 'pointerdown', fn: () => void): unknown; off(e: 'pointerdown', fn: () => void): unknown }`. Add to InputLayer `bindCharacter(target: PointerTarget, id: string, onDown?: () => void): void`. Implement: create fn that, if active, emits phaserToReact 'characterClick' {id} then calls onDown?.(); call target.on('pointerdown', fn); push a remover `() => target.off('pointerdown', fn)` into a `releasers` array; in destroy() call and clear all releasers.
steps.expected: Layer binds and releases character clicks

steps.action: Replace `sprite.on(Phaser.Input.Events.POINTER_DOWN, () => {...})` with `this.inputLayer?.bindCharacter(sprite, spec.id, () => {...})` where the callback keeps the existing `if (!idleKey) return; ... sprite.play(interactKey); sprite.once(...)` body and drops the characterClick emit.
steps.expected: Pointer wiring is in the layer; typecheck passes
